correctness.finding: PASS. For diameter-two graphs, every nonzero geodesic is either an edge or an induced length-two path, so gpn(G)=n+m+p3. The auxiliary identity 2(m+p3)=sum_x e(N(x),V\N(x)) is correct: every edge is counted at its two endpoints and every induced P3 contributes exactly two additional endpoint-as-third-vertex crossings. Each cut has at most d(x)(n-d(x))<=floor(n^2/4), proving the bound. Equality forces every neighborhood cut to be complete and every degree to be a half-size; nonadjacency is then an equivalence relation, giving a complete multipartite graph, and the half-size condition leaves exactly balanced complete bipartite graphs for n>=4 (with K3 as the extra n=3 equality case for the auxiliary lemma, excluded by diameter two). Exhaustive independent enumeration of all labelled graphs through n=6 found no violation and exactly the expected equality graphs.

originality.finding: PASS, NARROWLY. Knor--Sedlar--Skrekovski--Zhang introduced gpn in 2026 and explicitly leave broad extremal questions open; their concluding discussion notes balanced complete bipartite graphs and that deleting a perfect matching can increase gpn, but it does not state the diameter-two extremal theorem. Pyatkin--Lykhovyd--Butenko proved the separate maximum of induced open triangles p3, with the same balanced complete-bipartite extremizer, but that result does not optimize the weighted quantity m+p3. Searches for the exact weighted inequality and diameter-two formulation did not locate prior art.

scientific_value.finding: PASS. The result exactly characterizes the maximum gpn and unique extremizer on the natural class of diameter-two graphs, and the weighted open-triangle inequality is an elementary reusable lemma. It also cleanly explains why the complete-bipartite family is extremal before the longer-geodesic phenomena that arise once diameter exceeds two.
